newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan expels anti-Taleban Afghan leaders.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan expels anti-Taleban Afghan leaders.

text.p: A former Afghan provincial governor said on Sunday that Pakistan had asked him and a colleague to leave the country because of activities against Afghanistan's dominant Taleban Islamic movement.

Haji Abdul Qadeer, the former governor of the eastern Afghan province of Nangarhar, told Reuters that he and former Nangarhar corps commander Haji Mohammad Zaman would leave Pakistan for Dubai on Monday, meeting a deadline set by Pakistani authorities, and would later go to their bases in Afghanistan.
No comment from the Pakistani government was immediately available.

"We were asked (on Wednesday) to stop our anti-Taleban activities in the eastern provinces or leave Pakistan within four days", said Qadeer, who headed a neutral council that ruled three eastern Afghan provinces until ousted by Taleban in September.
He said that he and Zaman had told Pakistani officials that they would not give up what he called their "revolution" against Taleban, which controls more than two-thirds of Afghanistan.
